historical_references.reference: According to the 'Golden Legend', Thalina was a Jewish princess who converted to Christianity and was martyred during the reign of Emperor Hadrian (117-138 AD). Her story is not found in early Christian texts and is likely a later invention.

In the 'Acts of Thalassius and Thala', a late antique Greek hagiography, Thalina is depicted as the sister of Thalassius and the wife of the Roman prefect Maximian. She was martyred along with her brother and husband during the reign of Emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD) for refusing to sacrifice to the Roman gods.
